title: Shave the Sum to a Multiple
statement:
You get an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer k. One operation picks any element and decreases it by 1. Elements may go down to 0 but never below.

Return the fewest operations needed to make the sum of nums divisible by k. A sum of 0 counts as divisible.

examples.why: The sum is 15. The nearest multiple of 4 at or below it is 12, three decrements away.
The sum 12 is already a multiple of 3.
The sum 3 is below k. The only reachable multiple is 0, so every element drops to 0.

hints: Only the sum matters, not which element you decrease.
Each operation lowers the sum by exactly 1. Which multiple of k should you aim for?
The nearest multiple at or below the sum is sum − (sum mod k). That is always reachable, because the sum can drop all the way to 0.

explain.intuition:
Every operation lowers the total by exactly one, no matter which element you touch, and you can never raise it. So you are walking the sum downward and want to stop at the first multiple of k. That is sum mod k steps away.

Could you run out of room? No. The elements can reach 0, so the sum can go anywhere from its value down to 0, and sum mod k ≤ sum.
pitfalls: Returning k − sum % k, which is the distance to the next multiple above. You can only go down.
Thinking you must decrease one specific element, or worrying that small elements block you. Any element works, and 0 is allowed.

solutions.title: Decrement until divisible
solutions.idea: Simulate: lower the sum one step at a time until it is a multiple of k.

solutions.title: Sum modulo k
solutions.idea: The distance down to the nearest multiple of k is the remainder.

followups: Operations may also increase an element by 1. What is the answer now?
Each element may be decreased at most once. Which question are you answering then? (Subset sum modulo k.)
lcTitle: Minimum Operations to Make Array Sum Divisible by K
